references.finding: Set an ADI of 3 mg/kg bw/day for curcumin, from a NOAEL of 250-320 mg/kg bw/day (lower F2 body-weight gain in a reproductive toxicity study) with a 100-fold uncertainty factor; not carcinogenic or genotoxic.

references.authors: Fang W, Nasir Y
references.title: The effect of curcumin supplementation on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered creatine kinase (-48.5 IU/L) and muscle-soreness scores (WMD -0.48) after damaging exercise.

references.authors: Ferguson JJA, Abbott KA, Garg ML
references.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of oral supplementation with curcumin: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered CRP (-1.55 mg/L), IL-6 (-1.69 pg/mL) and TNF-a; authors note dose, duration and formulation remain unresolved.

references.authors: Flory S, Sus N, Haas K, et al.
references.title: Increasing Post-Digestive Solubility of Curcumin Is the Most Successful Strategy to Improve its Oral Bioavailability: A Randomized Cross-Over Trial in Healthy Adults and In Vitro Bioaccessibility Experiments.
references.finding: Head-to-head test of 8 formulations at 207 mg curcumin: no free curcumin was detected in anyone; only micelles (57-fold) and gamma-cyclodextrin (30-fold) significantly raised conjugate AUC; piperine-type adjuvants did not.

references.authors: Forsyth JE, Nurunnahar S, Islam SS, et al.
references.title: Turmeric means "yellow" in Bengali: Lead chromate pigments added to turmeric threaten public health across Bangladesh.
references.finding: Lead chromate pigment (2-10% lead by weight) is added to turmeric during polishing in 7 of 9 major producing districts of Bangladesh to meet demand for bright yellow colour.

references.authors: Forsyth JE, Mistree D, Nash E, et al.
references.title: Evidence of turmeric adulteration with lead chromate across South Asia.
references.finding: 14% of turmeric samples from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal had detectable lead (>2 ug/g); some exceeded 1000 ug/g with 1:1 lead:chromium ratios indicating lead chromate.

references.authors: Garcea G, Berry DP, Jones DJ, et al.
references.title: Consumption of the putative chemopreventive agent curcumin by cancer patients: assessment of curcumin levels in the colorectum and their pharmacodynamic consequences.
references.finding: 3.6 g/day curcumin for 7 days gave colorectal tissue curcumin of ~8-13 nmol/g and lowered M1G DNA adducts in tissue: the gut wall is the one site where gram doses reach meaningful levels.

references.authors: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, et al.
references.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN].
references.finding: US DILIN turmeric liver-injury cases rose since 2011; typically hepatocellular after 1-4 months, one death, 3 of 7 tested products contained piperine, and 7 of 10 patients carried HLA-B*35:01.

references.authors: Houghton CA, Fassett RG, Coombes JS
references.title: Sulforaphane and Other Nutrigenomic Nrf2 Activators: Can the Clinician's Expectation Be Matched by the Reality?
references.finding: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2 more potently and is far more bioavailable than curcumin, silymarin or resveratrol.

references.authors: Hu S, Belcaro G, Dugall M, et al.
references.title: Interaction study between antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement therapy and a bioavailable formulation of curcumin (Meriva®).
references.n: patients on antiplatelets, anticoagulants, levothyroxine or metformin
references.finding: 10-15 days of Meriva did not change bleeding time on aspirin/clopidogrel/ticlopidine, INR on warfarin or dabigatran, thyroid tests or glycaemia; short, uncontrolled, sponsor-linked.

references.authors: Jäger R, Lowery RP, Calvanese AV, et al.
references.title: Comparative absorption of curcumin formulations.
references.finding: Relative to standard curcumin, total curcuminoid exposure was 1.3-fold higher with turmeric-oil formulation, 7.9-fold with phytosome and 45.9-fold with a hydrophilic-carrier formulation (CHC).

references.authors: Jiao Y, Wilkinson J 4th, Di X, et al.
references.title: Curcumin, a cancer chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic agent, is a biologically active iron chelator.
references.finding: In mice with marginal iron intake, dietary curcumin acted as an iron chelator, lowered hepcidin and caused iron-deficiency anaemia.

references.authors: Kavyani Z, Najafi K, Naghsh N, et al.
references.title: The effects of curcumin supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial function: A meta-analysis of meta-analyses.
references.finding: Umbrella analysis: curcumin lowered CRP (-0.87 mg/L), IL-6, TNF-a and MDA, raised SOD, GPx, catalase and FMD (+1.64%), but did not significantly change TAC.

references.authors: Kocher A, Bohnert L, Schiborr C, et al.
references.title: Highly bioavailable micellar curcuminoids accumulate in blood, are safe and do not reduce blood lipids and inflammation markers in moderately hyperlipidemic individuals.
references.finding: 294 mg/day micellar curcuminoids for 6 weeks reached fasting plasma ~49 nmol/L but did not change lipids, CRP or other inflammation markers versus placebo.

references.authors: Kuptniratsaikul V, Dajpratham P, Taechaarpornkul W, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of Curcuma domestica extracts compared with ibuprofen in patients with knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter study.
references.finding: Curcuma domestica extract 1500 mg/day was non-inferior to ibuprofen 1200 mg/day over 4 weeks on WOMAC, with fewer abdominal complaints.

references.authors: Kusuhara H, Furuie H, Inano A, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetic interaction study of sulphasalazine in healthy subjects and the impact of curcumin as an in vivo inhibitor of BCRP.
references.finding: 2 g curcumin inhibited intestinal BCRP and raised sulfasalazine exposure 2.0-3.2-fold in humans.

references.authors: Lombardi N, Crescioli G, Maggini V, et al.
references.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports.
references.finding: Italian phytovigilance cases of acute (mostly cholestatic) hepatitis were all linked to high-bioavailability, high-dose curcumin products; positive dechallenge in most.

references.authors: Mahale J, Singh R, Howells LM, et al.
references.title: Detection of Plasma Curcuminoids from Dietary Intake of Turmeric-Containing Food in Human Volunteers.
references.finding: After a turmeric-containing meal at South Asian culinary levels, curcumin glucuronide peaked at ~48 nM and free curcumin was detectable (3.2 nM) in only one volunteer.

references.authors: Menniti-Ippolito F, Ippoliti I, Pastorelli AA, et al.
references.title: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) food supplements and hepatotoxicity: an integrated evaluation approach.
references.finding: A 2019 Italian cluster of 28 acute hepatitis reports linked to turmeric supplements; product testing looked for drugs, metals, aflatoxins, dyes and pyrrolizidine alkaloids, and regulators intervened.

references.authors: Musso G, Pinach S, Mariano F, et al.
references.title: Effect of phospholipid curcumin Meriva on liver histology and kidney disease in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
references.finding: Meriva 2 g/day for 72 weeks: NASH resolution in 62% vs 12% on placebo and fibrosis improvement in 50% vs 8%; single trial, needs replication.

references.authors: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, et al.
references.title: The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin.
references.finding: Argues curcumin is a PAINS/IMPS compound that is chemically unstable, reactive and not bioavailable; states that no double-blind placebo-controlled curcumin trial had been successful as of 2017.

references.authors: Ng TP, Chiam PC, Lee T, et al.
references.title: Curry consumption and cognitive function in the elderly.
references.finding: Occasional or frequent curry eaters had better MMSE scores than never/rare eaters (cross-sectional association, confounding possible).

references.authors: Pal A, Sung B, Bhanu Prasad BA, et al.
references.title: Curcumin glucuronides: assessing the proliferative activity against human cell lines.
references.finding: Curcumin killed cancer cell lines at 1-10 uM, but its mono- and di-glucuronides (the main circulating forms) showed no antiproliferative activity.

references.authors: Pattanaik S, Hota D, Prabhakar S, et al.
references.title: Effect of piperine on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of phenytoin in patients with epilepsy.
references.finding: A single 20 mg piperine dose significantly raised phenytoin AUC and Cmax at steady state.

references.authors: US National Library of Medicine
references.title: PubMed searches 'Aggarwal BB[au] AND retracted publication[pt]' and 'curcumin AND retracted publication[pt]', run 2026-10-01 via NCBI E-utilities.
references.finding: Returned 27 retracted publications with BB Aggarwal as author and 162 retracted publications mentioning curcumin.

references.authors: Purpura M, Lowery RP, Wilson JM, et al.
references.title: Analysis of different innovative formulations of curcumin for improved relative oral bioavailability in human subjects.
references.finding: A gamma-cyclodextrin curcumin complex gave 39-fold higher total curcuminoid AUC than unformulated extract, exceeding a phytosome and a turmeric-oil formulation.

references.authors: Qin S, Huang L, Gong J, et al.
references.title: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of 4 weeks or longer suggest that curcumin may afford some protection against oxidative stress.
references.finding: Curcumin >=4 weeks lowered MDA (SMD -0.77) and raised SOD (SMD 1.08) with no change in RBC GPx; the MDA effect appeared at >=600 mg/day curcuminoids.

references.authors: Rasyid A, Rahman AR, Jaalam K, et al.
references.title: Effect of different curcumin dosages on human gall bladder.
references.finding: Curcumin 20, 40 and 80 mg contracted the gallbladder by 34%, 51% and 72% within 2 h.

references.authors: Ringman JM, Frautschy SA, Teng E, et al.
references.title: Oral curcumin for Alzheimer's disease: tolerability and efficacy in a 24-week randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study.
references.finding: Curcumin C3 Complex 2 or 4 g/day for 24 weeks showed no clinical or biomarker benefit; native plasma curcumin was low (7.3 ng/mL) and 3 withdrew for GI symptoms.

references.authors: Ristow M, Zarse K, Oberbach A, et al.
references.title: Antioxidants prevent health-promoting effects of physical exercise in humans.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Vitamin C 1000 mg plus vitamin E 400 IU/day blocked exercise-induced gains in insulin sensitivity and induction of endogenous antioxidant defences.

references.authors: Ryan Wolf J, Heckler CE, Guido JJ, et al.
references.title: Oral curcumin for radiation dermatitis: a URCC NCORP study of 686 breast cancer patients.
references.finding: Oral curcumin 6 g/day during radiotherapy did not reduce radiation dermatitis severity versus placebo.

references.authors: Schiborr C, Kocher A, Behnam D, et al.
references.title: The oral bioavailability of curcumin from micronized powder and liquid micelles is significantly increased in healthy humans and differs between sexes.
references.finding: Single 500 mg dose: micronized curcumin was 9-fold and liquid micellar curcumin 185-fold more bioavailable (AUC) than native powder; women absorbed more than men.

references.authors: Shin JW, Chun KS, Kim DH, et al.
references.title: Curcumin induces stabilization of Nrf2 protein through Keap1 cysteine modification.
references.finding: In mouse skin and epidermal cells, curcumin binds KEAP1 Cys151 and stabilises Nrf2 to induce HO-1; tetrahydrocurcumin, which lacks the Michael-acceptor group, does not.

references.authors: Shoba G, Joy D, Joseph T, et al.
references.title: Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers.
references.finding: 2 g curcumin alone gave undetectable or very low serum levels; with 20 mg piperine bioavailability (AUC) rose about 2000%.

references.authors: Small GW, Siddarth P, Li Z, et al.
references.title: Memory and Brain Amyloid and Tau Effects of a Bioavailable Form of Curcumin in Non-Demented Adults: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled 18-Month Trial.
references.finding: Theracurmin 90 mg curcumin twice daily for 18 months improved verbal and visual memory and attention versus placebo and lowered FDDNP-PET signal in amygdala/hypothalamus; very small trial.

references.authors: Stohs SJ, Chen CYO, Preuss HG, et al.
references.title: The fallacy of enzymatic hydrolysis for the determination of bioactive curcumin in plasma samples as an indication of bioavailability: a comparative study.
references.finding: Most curcumin PK studies hydrolyse plasma before analysis and so report total (free plus conjugated) curcumin, which overstates the bioactive free fraction.

references.authors: Tang M, Larson-Meyer DE, Liebman M
references.title: Effect of cinnamon and turmeric on urinary oxalate excretion, plasma lipids, and plasma glucose in healthy subjects.
references.finding: Supplemental turmeric raised urinary oxalate excretion (91% of its oxalate is soluble) and did not change glucose or lipids over 4 weeks.

references.authors: Tayyem RF, Heath DD, Al-Delaimy WK, et al.
references.title: Curcumin content of turmeric and curry powders.
references.finding: HPLC of 28 spice products: pure turmeric powder averaged 3.14% curcumin by weight; most curry powders contained little and variable curcumin.

references.authors: Tuntipopipat S, Judprasong K, Zeder C, et al.
references.title: Chili, but not turmeric, inhibits iron absorption in young women from an iron-fortified composite meal.
references.finding: 0.5 g turmeric in a meal did not inhibit iron absorption (stable isotopes), whereas chili cut it by 38%.

references.authors: Vareed SK, Kakarala M, Ruffin MT, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of curcumin conjugate metabolites in healthy human subjects.
references.finding: After 10 or 12 g curcumin, free curcumin was detectable in only one subject; glucuronide and sulfate conjugates were found in all (Cmax ~1.7-2.3 ug/mL).

references.authors: Wang Z, Jones G, Winzenberg T, et al.
references.title: Effectiveness of Curcuma longa Extract for the Treatment of Symptoms and Effusion-Synovitis of Knee Osteoarthritis : A Randomized Trial.
references.n: 70 adults with knee OA and effusion-synovitis
references.finding: Curcuma longa extract (2 capsules/day, 12 weeks) cut VAS knee pain by 9.1 mm versus placebo but did not change effusion-synovitis volume or cartilage; funded partly by the manufacturer.

references.authors: Wang Z, Singh A, Jones G, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and Safety of Turmeric Extracts for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Turmeric extracts reduced knee OA pain (SMD -0.82) and improved function versus placebo, similar to NSAIDs; very high heterogeneity, moderate risk of bias, less benefit with higher BMI.
